annotation.summary: Argues that scientific progress is not a continuous accumulation of facts but a sequence of paradigms — frameworks of theory, instrumentation, and practice — punctuated by revolutionary shifts when anomalies overwhelm the prevailing paradigm.
annotation.method: Historical analysis across physics, chemistry, and astronomy, surveying episodes such as the Copernican shift, the chemical revolution, and the rise of relativity. Concept-driven rather than empirical in any quantitative sense.
annotation.evaluation: Influential but contested. The notion of incommensurability is doing a lot of work and has been criticized as overstating discontinuity between paradigms. Useful as a vocabulary even where one disagrees with the conclusions.
annotation.relevance: Background for our methodology chapter; cite when discussing why disciplinary communities resist new measurement frameworks.
